title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Rolling a Contract's Futures Month at the Member's Instruction
content:
A member who wants the futures month referenced by a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts moved disposes of their own grain position in doing so. The result governed is the charge the roll carries to the member, written onto the member's grain ledger as one roll confirmation against the named contract, so that the charge stands to be collected with the member's grain money.

The charge a roll carries is fixed only after the bushels still owed on the contract stand at the figure the loads applied to it support.

**Capability.** The call writes one roll confirmation onto the member's grain ledger for the named contract, carrying the charge the roll costs them; the contract's programme, commodity, committed bushels and lifecycle standing are left as they stand.

**How it is invoked, and by whom.** The recorded act is `execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f`. A roll disposes of the member's own grain position, so it is not the desk's act to perform: the grain desk unlocks it and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves, the member whose position is being rolled, against the roll instruction they have signed.

**The parameters it takes.**

- `contract_id` — the internal reference of the grain marketing contract being rolled; it identifies one contract record and is reachable from the grain contract lookup for the member before this call.
- `customer_id` — the internal reference of the member whose position is rolled; it identifies one membership record and is reachable from the membership profile lookup before this call.
- `pricing_order_id` — the internal reference of the signed roll instruction the member lodged with the grain desk; it identifies one instruction record and is reachable from the pricing instruction lookup for the member before this call.
- `roll_charge_amount_usd` — the charge the roll carries to the member, in USD to 2 decimal places, as a positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator, rounded half away from zero at the cent when a longer value is supplied.

**What comes back.** A single confirmation sentence in plain text naming the ledger line reference minted for the roll, the contract it was written against, and the charge carried in USD to 2 decimal places; that sentence, rather than an error text, is what indicates the roll was recorded.
